data.title: bn-21ew: direct outcomes and bounded owner scratch (implementation)
data.description: risk:high — failure-mode checklist required. Refute merge-readiness for implementation commit 68434ad. Attack: exact callback ordering and once-only completion across Process, Os, and Group; ordered-unit partial success; all-input preflight before registry/domain writes; EIO, ENOSPC, roll, sticky poison, watermark and barrier invariants; bounded retained request/effect/index/outcome scratch under oversized input; callback/index panic surfaces; unchanged async Ack allocation/layout/semantics; cancellation-safe publication; metric accuracy and benchmark evidence. Please answer: 1) What failure modes exist? 2) What edge cases need validation? 3) How can we roll back if this breaks? 4) What monitoring/alerts should we add? 5) What input validation is needed?

data.body: HIGH: The candidate has not satisfied its frozen measurement contract. GATES.md says barrier counts may not change / may not increase, but the final ABBA evidence records Group b1 at 4,823 candidate vs 4,821 baseline and b10 at 3,023 vs 3,022, and labels both rows 'fail literal barrier total'. Lines 139-140 correctly call the matrix a non-pass, but the only follow-up study is scoped to Os b1/b10 p99 and therefore cannot close these Group barrier failures. Tiny deltas may well be scheduling variance (the all-cell Group total is exactly equal), but accepting that post hoc would rewrite the predeclared rule. Before merge, add a predeclared, reproducible Group-specific variance/parity study (or a deterministic fixed-admission barrier-parity test) that closes this gate, retain the raw rows, and update the report with the explicit decision rule and result. If it does not pass, decline/rework the candidate.

LOW: The public metric documentation is inaccurate: direct_scratch_retained_bytes is described as request/effect storage, but the implementation also sums DirectIndex capacity. This is conservative rather than unsafe, yet operators cannot interpret the field precisely. Rename/document it as request/effect/index storage in both the internal and public comments.

data.reason: Frozen performance gate remains open: final Group b1/b10 barrier counts increased, and the Os-only variance study does not close that failure. Static correctness review found no separate blocking lifecycle defect, but this measurement-driven bone is not merge-ready until Group barrier parity/non-regression is established under a predeclared rule.

data.body: Fixed in exact HEAD 380f7135. The study/rule was committed before measurement at 7035ae9a: only Group b1/b10, five complete ABBA cycles, candidate aggregate <= baseline and median cycle delta <= 0 independently per cell, exact event assertion, any failure declines. Then exactly 40 rows ran with no retries/extra cells. b1 baseline/candidate 8039/8036, deltas [-1,-1,+1,-1,-1], median -1; b10 5036/5036, deltas [+1,0,-2,0,+1], median 0. Raw BN-21EW-GROUP-PARITY-ABBA.csv and binary/source/load provenance are committed; report retains the earlier literal failure and explains why this predeclared paired result admits the scheduling variance without widening the gate.
Fixed at 7035ae9a (included in exact HEAD 380f7135): both internal and public direct_scratch_retained_bytes comments now say request/effect/index bytes.
